description: Pins DeskOS keeps by hand: the platform bootc base image (tag + digest),
the binary artifacts of the example. The scanner and action pins in the
workflows move by hand too, because the token cannot write there.
The Dockerfile/actions managers from config:recommended cover the rest.
NOTE: a binary artifact has a sha256 that Renovate cannot compute, so its
PR bumps the version only and the checksum must be filled before merge;
the CentOS Stream 10 base-image digest IS updated automatically, while the
RHEL 10 one is moved by hand (see the packageRules below). The Samba DC
fixture is ignored: it installs Samba from Fedora at build time, so its base
digest is a disposable test input, bumped by hand. Action versions
are bumped by hand too, for the same reason the token has no workflows

packageRules.description: Base images and scanners: review before merging

Fedora publishes the next release number as the rawhide tag: registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora:46 is rawhide, not a release (the identity fixture is the Samba DC, which follows the released line). Major tag bumps are never proposed; digest moves on the current tag still are.

The RHEL 10 base image needs a Red Hat subscription to list its tags and refuses anonymous reads; this repository carries no subscription credential, so that digest is a deliberate, hand-made move. Disabled here so the dashboard does not show a permanent lookup failure.

Action versions are bumped by hand: RENOVATE_TOKEN deliberately lacks the workflows permission, so Renovate could not commit a change under .github/workflows, and a token that can edit a workflow can run arbitrary code beside this repository's registry credentials. Disabled so the dashboard shows no error.

The Syft and Grype tags in image-publish.yml are moved by hand for the same reason: a change under .github/workflows is a change the token cannot push. The custom managers stay for the day the token gains the scope, but they are disabled so the dashboard shows no permanent error.
